# The Glass Teletype: A History of Terminal Emulators

Every time a developer opens a terminal window on a laptop, they are running a program that pretends to be a piece of hardware that has not been manufactured in decades. The blinking cursor, the fixed-width grid of characters, the escape sequences that change colors and move the cursor around: all of these are echoes of physical machines that once sat on desks, humming and clattering, wired to mainframes and minicomputers in distant rooms. The terminal emulator is one of the most durable pieces of software in computing history, and its story is a story of layered compatibility, where each generation preserves the quirks of the last.

## Before the screen
